text:
maya: heads up — after merging cust-hyperion-lora into base-13b and running int4 quant on the merge, we see embedding collapse on the customer prompt set. quick looked at samples: outputs are short, repetitive, and embeddings norm ~0.02 across prompts. did anyone see tokenizer/merge warnings when applying the lora?

tom: saw this on a test earlier — usually token mismatch or pad token override. did you compare tokenizer configs between base and lora?

maya: good call. the lora metadata claims no tokenizer changes, but the merge script log shows `tokenizer.json` overwritten. snippet: ```
Merging weights...
Overwriting file: tokenizer.json
Applied lora -> base_v13b
```

anita: ugh. that explains it. hyperion's finetune had a subtle BPE merge that introduces an extra special token for their product codes ("<prd>"). If tokenizer got overwritten we could have new token ids remapped — embeddings collapse when common tokens shift.

maya: @anita can you confirm what token id shift looks like? any quick check commands I should run?

anita: run this locally against both tokenizers: ```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
a = Tokenizer.from_file('base_v13b/tokenizer.json')
b = Tokenizer.from_file('merged/tokenizer.json')
print(a.encode('product code: 12345').ids)
print(b.encode('product code: 12345').ids)
```
If ids differ for frequent punctuation/words that's a red flag.

tom: also check embedding matrix row for the token id before vs after. if the embedding vector points to a random new id, norms will be tiny after quant / alignment.

qa-bot: quick-eval-pack run summary attached: 50 prompts from hyperion, metrics: embs_cos_mean=0.12 (baseline 0.78), response_entropy down 45%, average length 6 tokens (baseline 41). Fail threshold tripped.

maya: thanks @qa-bot. i'm re-running the tokenizer compare now.

(an hour later)

maya: confirmed — tokenizer overwritten. base had no <prd> token; merged assigned <prd> id 50267 which shifted some nearby ids. embedding row 50267 is near-zero after int4 quant.

anita: recommendation: revert tokenizer file in the merge, re-run merge but whitelist lora weight files only (no tokenizer, no vocab). We should also add a pre-merge check that fails if `tokenizer.json` would be replaced.

tom: agreed. for immediate mitigation: rollback the hyperion model in hosted and deploy previous artifact. Use canary route and pin customers to v13b+hyperion-lora@rollback until we republish.

devops-bot: deploy rollback initiated: `rollback artifact hyperion-lora:2026-03-15` -> started on dedicated pool us-west-2. ETA ~7m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: i'm packaging a quick-eval fix pack that excludes tokenizer and vocab, only includes delta weights. will push PR to `cust-hyperion/lora` with tests.

anita: add an automated test in our merge CI: `git diff --name-only` should fail if tokenizer.json or vocab* present. sample rule: `if any(f in changed for f in ['tokenizer.json','vocab.json','merges.txt']): exit 1`.

tom: also add a post-merge sanity run: sample 20 prompts, compute embedding norm distribution; if median_norm < 0.1 or cos_mean < 0.5 then fail. run on both fp16 and int4 quant sim.

maya: will do. i'll also include a short note to the SRE oncall about the rollback and customer impact. @tom can you follow-up with Hyperion's SE so they know we're reverting and re-publishing?

tom: on it. pinging them now.

qa-bot: re-run of quick-eval after rollback (canary) shows embs_cos_mean=0.77, response_entropy restored. passing smoke suite. :white_check_mark:

maya: huge thanks everyone. follow-ups: 1) PR to prevent tokenizer overwrite; 2) CI embedding-norm check; 3) updated runbook for cust merges. i'll open tickets.

anita: add a note in the merge docs about never shipping tokenizer unless explicit opt-in (and requiring SE sign-off).

tom: logging here for postmortem: root cause = tokenizer file included in LoRA bundle -> id remap -> int4 quant amplified tiny embedding rows -> collapse. mitigation implemented + CI guards.

maya: closing loop — I'll attach the quick-eval pack and the failing logs to the ticket. thanks all. :raised_hands:
